statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Weekend venue closure with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail remains far below the block threshold while Stress stays elevated on rates and energy.
recommendation: Conditions map to EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Risk is concentrated in the narrow 22:00-02:00 UTC futures-reopen window rather than across the session; existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Closed weekend tape, elevated Stress: hawkish payroll repricing and fresh Hormuz escalation meet a thin Sunday reopen
body: CME equity futures have been closed since Friday 21:00 UTC, so no live Nasdaq-100 price path is observable at this assessment. The last verified tape is Friday September 4: ^NDX closed 29,544.15 (+0.21%) inside a 29,440.15-29,655.22 range, a mid-range finish with no session-extreme hold, while VIX ended near 14.53. The Nasdaq Composite fell 0.29% and the S&P 500 0.38% as the August employment report printed 162,000 payrolls against roughly 55,000 consensus, lifting Treasury yields and firming pricing for a hike at the September 15-16 FOMC. H.15 showed the 2-year at 4.34% and the 10-year at 4.77% as of September 3, before Friday's move. Over the weekend the US-Iran conflict escalated in the Strait of Hormuz: US forces destroyed three Iranian crude carriers after missile fire at US warships, the IRGC claimed strikes on three US-affiliated vessels and three tankers, and Tehran threatened more severe attacks while a naval blockade persists. Brent finished the week near $96 with a gain above 7% and WTI near $91 in its strongest week since mid-July. That combination raises Stress materially, but the strategy-relevant failure mode requires an observed no-retracement price path, and none exists: Friday closed mid-range, VIX stayed under 15, and cross-asset signals conflict rather than align, with semiconductors firm against weaker software. Tail therefore stays low. Conditional risk concentrates at the 22:00 UTC futures reopen, when two days of escalation are repriced into the thinnest depth of the week ahead of a US Labor Day holiday that keeps cash markets shut on Monday. Even there the profile stays inside the low band, because a wider gap distribution is not the same as a sustained one-way trend, and Sunday gaps more often mean-revert than extend.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly Claude assessments are available. Tail held flat at 4-5 with EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress climbed from 38 during Friday's European session to a 57 peak around the U.S. close as the payroll beat lifted yields, then eased to 52-56 across the weekend closure. Dominant mode stayed normal for every hour.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours cover roughly 14 further closed hours, the 22:00 UTC futures reopen, and an Asian session on a US Labor Day holiday. Conditional Tail stays inside the low band throughout, peaking at 18 in the reopen hour where two days of verified Hormuz escalation meet the thinnest depth of the week, then decaying toward 8 as two-way discovery is assumed to resume. Stress peaks near 66 at the reopen on the combined rates and energy backdrop. No US macro release falls inside the window; the next scheduled checkpoints are August PPI on September 10 and August CPI on September 11, both at 12:30 UTC, ahead of the September 15-16 FOMC.
